bull_bear.body:
- Only manufacturer of AlF3 in Andhra Pradesh and one of the few domestic producers qualified to supply high-purity, low-bulk-density material to every major primary aluminium smelter in India, including Hindalco, Vedanta and NALCO
- High switching barriers: smelter qualification is a slow, exacting process, and an off-specification consignment can damage potlines that are expensive and time-consuming to restart, so established supplier relationships, quality consistency and delivery reliability - not price alone - determine retention of business
- External validation of customer standing: Hindalco Resilient Supply Chain Award (November 2024) and NALCO Best Customer (Chemical Division) Award (March 2025)
- Coastal Visakhapatnam plant location within manageable freight range of every major Indian smelter and on the same coast as both principal FSA suppliers, keeping outbound logistics efficient
- Captive solar power (expanded to 4.1 MW in May 2026) lowers the cost of conversion and the Company's carbon footprint
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Raw-material (FSA) supply concentration and geopolitical exposure — FSA, the Company's key raw material, is sourced principally from IFFCO Paradeep and supplemented by Paradeep Phosphates and Coromandel International's phosphoric acid plants; all suppliers ultimately depend on imported rock phosphate, sulphur and ammonia routed via the Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea. Intensifying West Asia hostilities have, since late FY2025-26, constrained the upstream sulphur/ammonia chain and the downstream FSA byproduct, forcing the Company to disclose a production scale-back to exchanges on 23 May 2026 with a financial impact management calls 'not presently determinable'.
- Customer concentration — Primary aluminium smelting capacity has consolidated among fewer, larger operators; the largest customer accounted for 69.27% of AlF3 revenue in FY2024-25, up sharply from 52.51% in FY2023-24, while the share from other 10%+ customers (excluding the top two) fell from 20.40% to nil, leaving the Company reliant on a small number of buyers.
- Single-product / single-activity concentration — The Company manufactures a single product line, Aluminium Fluoride, with no separate segment reporting under Ind AS 108; the ancillary solar power activity is immaterial to revenue and entirely dependent on captive consumption, leaving overall performance tied to one product and its input/output market dynamics.
- Cyclicality of the primary aluminium industry — Demand for AlF3 is transmitted through customers' offtake patterns in the primary aluminium industry, exposing the Company to that industry's cyclicality even though its own qualification-based customer relationships are sticky.
- Freight and logistics cost exposure — A portion of the Company's FSA requirement is moved over a longer distance from Odisha, and the associated inland freight cost is absorbed by the Company rather than passed through, an increase in which is flagged as a recurring risk.
- Input cost inflation (fuel, power, consumables) and foreign-exchange volatility — The Company is exposed to increases in the cost of fuel, power and consumables, and to foreign-exchange volatility on the limited proportion of imported inputs and capital goods.
- Operational hazard risk (fire, environmental incident, industrial accident) — Management flags the customary risks of fire, environmental incident and industrial accident at its manufacturing operations as a recurring risk category, against which it maintains insurance cover; the Board's overall view is that no material risk threatens the Company's existence.

Alongside this single product line, the Company runs a small captive solar power generation activity, used mainly for captive consumption with surplus units sold to the grid.

business.body:
- Only manufacturer of AlF3 in Andhra Pradesh and one of the few domestic producers qualified to supply high-purity, low-bulk-density material to every major primary aluminium smelter in India, including Hindalco, Vedanta and NALCO
- High switching barriers: smelter qualification is a slow, exacting process, and an off-specification consignment can damage potlines that are expensive and time-consuming to restart, so established supplier relationships, quality consistency and delivery reliability - not price alone - determine retention of business
- External validation of customer standing: Hindalco Resilient Supply Chain Award (November 2024) and NALCO Best Customer (Chemical Division) Award (March 2025)
- Coastal Visakhapatnam plant location within manageable freight range of every major Indian smelter and on the same coast as both principal FSA suppliers, keeping outbound logistics efficient
- Captive solar power (expanded to 4.1 MW in May 2026) lowers the cost of conversion and the Company's carbon footprint
business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Backward integration into Alumina Hydrate (the second principal input into AlF3 manufacture) via a proposed greenfield facility, to reduce exposure to procurement-cost volatility and extend the Company's presence further upstream in the aluminium value chain as a separate vertical
- Diversifying the FSA (raw material) supplier base beyond IFFCO Paradeep to include Paradeep Phosphates and Coromandel International's phosphoric acid plants at Visakhapatnam and, from April 2026, Kakinada, to reduce concentration risk on a single supplier
- Diversifying the customer base and reducing customer concentration by pursuing qualification of additional buyers and developing overseas markets through the wholly owned subsidiary Alufluoride International Pte. Ltd., Singapore
- Evaluating other domestic and overseas growth opportunities including potential second-site AlF3 capacity, adjacent fluorine-derivative chemistries, transport of the Company's raw materials via Electric Vehicles, and value-added products from silica (a byproduct of AlF3 manufacture) - all at an assessment stage pending Board satisfaction on project specifications, capital cost, financing and revenue economics
- Continuing the phased capacity build-out at Visakhapatnam to match the medium-term capacity expansion trajectory announced by principal smelter customers
- Deploying retained earnings primarily towards capacity expansion, backward integration and strengthening of the working-capital position, alongside a policy of progressively growing shareholder distributions
- Maintaining captive solar power generation to keep conversion cost low and contain the Company's carbon footprint
- Exited the AlF3 joint venture in Jordan (withdrawal initiated FY2024-25, completed during FY2025-26) in response to the deteriorating West Asia political environment and a Jordanian-bank requirement for a parent corporate guarantee
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company has expanded its AlF3 manufacturing capacity at Visakhapatnam in phases: 4,000 TPA at commissioning; 8,000 TPA through debottlenecking over the years; 12,000 TPA in a second phase; 18,000 TPA in a subsequent debottlenecking; and 24,000 TPA on completion of the final phase in June 2026. A further expansion of AlF3 production infrastructure, undertaken in anticipation of increased FSA (raw material) availability, was targeted for completion by end of June 2026 and is stated to give the enhanced facility a production capacity of 80 tons per day (TPD). Separately, the Company is exploring a greenfield Alumina Hydrate manufacturing facility as a backward-integration and diversification project (objects clause amended via postal ballot on 20 April 2025), and is evaluating other domestic and overseas opportunities including potential second-site AlF3 capacity, adjacent fluorine-derivative chemistries, transport of raw materials via Electric Vehicles, and value-added products from silica (an AlF3 byproduct) - all at an early assessment stage. On the raw-material supply side, Coromandel International's new phosphoric acid plant at Kakinada began supplying FSA to the Company from April 2026, diversifying the supplier base alongside the existing long-term IFFCO Paradeep arrangement. The captive solar power facility (3 MW commissioned in 2021) was expanded by a further 1.1 MW to 4.1 MW in May 2026. During the year, Punjab National Bank sanctioned an additional term loan of INR 20.22 crore to fund further expansion of AlF3 production facilities.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- The structural demand outlook for AlF3 remains favourable: Indian primary aluminium smelting capacity continues to expand, with each of the Company's principal customers having announced material capacity additions over the medium term
- AlF3 production grew at a compound annual rate of approximately 9% between FY2022-23 and FY2024-25, with FY2024-25 production and dispatches at all-time highs, and FY2025-26 carrying that trajectory forward
- The Company's qualification status with its principal customers is current and active, and its FSA supply arrangements are, in normal conditions, sufficient to support installed AlF3 capacity
- In the immediate term, the FSA supply disruption from the West Asia conflict is expected to concentrate its volume impact in Q1 FY2026-27, with Q2 expected to recover towards the prior-year production level as FSA availability improves; the Board expects H1 FY2026-27 as a whole to show some reduction in AlF3 volumes relative to a normal period
- The Company has limited its input-cost exposure for the disrupted period by finalising procurement contracts only after the onset of the disruption, affording a degree of pricing protection, and expects operating economics to revert to the pre-disruption pattern once normal FSA supply resumes
- Notwithstanding near-term FSA-related production risk, the Company remains optimistic about delivering improved FY2026-27 financial performance, supported by increased production volumes, agreed realization prices, and enhanced operational efficiencies
- Customer concentration (largest customer at 69.27% of FY2024-25 AlF3 revenue) is attributed by the Board to consolidation of demand among a smaller number of larger primary aluminium operators, rather than to any weakening of the Company's commercial position
- The Company deferred finalisation of its latest sales contracts until May 2026, securing agreed realization prices that afford a measure of protection against the raw-material cost increases seen earlier in the disruption period; no explicit order-book value or volume was disclosed.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: The only manufacturer of aluminium fluoride (AlF3) in Andhra Pradesh and one of a handful of domestic producers qualified to supply every major primary aluminium smelter in India, including Hindalco, Vedanta and NALCO.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Alufluoride Limited manufactures aluminium fluoride (AlF3), a specialty fluorine chemical used as a flux by primary aluminium smelters in the electrolytic reduction of alumina, converting hydro-fluosilicic acid (FSA) - a byproduct of phosphatic fertiliser manufacture - into high-purity AlF3 for smelter customers across India. Alongside this single product line, the Company runs a small captive solar power generation activity, used mainly for captive consumption with surplus units sold to the grid.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- Alufluoride International Pte. Ltd., Singapore — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary of the Company, incorporated in Singapore; reports in USD; disclosed in Form AOC-1 and as a related party under Ind AS 24
- M/s Anar Enterprises Pvt. Ltd. — related party: Entity in which key management personnel and/or their close relatives have a significant interest; a shareholder receiving dividend
- M/s Kaiser Finance and Leasing Pvt. Ltd. — related party: Entity in which key management personnel and/or their close relatives have a significant interest; a shareholder receiving dividend
- M/s Visakha Finance Pvt. Ltd. — related party: Entity in which key management personnel and/or their close relatives have a significant interest; a shareholder receiving dividend

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Aluminium Fluoride:** Aluminium Fluoride (AlF3)
- **Power:** Captive solar power (grid surplus sale)

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body: Indian primary aluminium smelters (domestic market; no export sales registered in the current or previous year)

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- The structural demand outlook for AlF3 remains favourable: Indian primary aluminium smelting capacity continues to expand, with each of the Company's principal customers having announced material capacity additions over the medium term
- AlF3 production grew at a compound annual rate of approximately 9% between FY2022-23 and FY2024-25, with FY2024-25 production and dispatches at all-time highs, and FY2025-26 carrying that trajectory forward
- The Company's qualification status with its principal customers is current and active, and its FSA supply arrangements are, in normal conditions, sufficient to support installed AlF3 capacity
- In the immediate term, the FSA supply disruption from the West Asia conflict is expected to concentrate its volume impact in Q1 FY2026-27, with Q2 expected to recover towards the prior-year production level as FSA availability improves; the Board expects H1 FY2026-27 as a whole to show some reduction in AlF3 volumes relative to a normal period
- The Company has limited its input-cost exposure for the disrupted period by finalising procurement contracts only after the onset of the disruption, affording a degree of pricing protection, and expects operating economics to revert to the pre-disruption pattern once normal FSA supply resumes
- Notwithstanding near-term FSA-related production risk, the Company remains optimistic about delivering improved FY2026-27 financial performance, supported by increased production volumes, agreed realization prices, and enhanced operational efficiencies
- Customer concentration (largest customer at 69.27% of FY2024-25 AlF3 revenue) is attributed by the Board to consolidation of demand among a smaller number of larger primary aluminium operators, rather than to any weakening of the Company's commercial position
- The Company deferred finalisation of its latest sales contracts until May 2026, securing agreed realization prices that afford a measure of protection against the raw-material cost increases seen earlier in the disruption period; no explicit order-book value or volume was disclosed.

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Backward integration into Alumina Hydrate (the second principal input into AlF3 manufacture) via a proposed greenfield facility, to reduce exposure to procurement-cost volatility and extend the Company's presence further upstream in the aluminium value chain as a separate vertical
- Diversifying the FSA (raw material) supplier base beyond IFFCO Paradeep to include Paradeep Phosphates and Coromandel International's phosphoric acid plants at Visakhapatnam and, from April 2026, Kakinada, to reduce concentration risk on a single supplier
- Diversifying the customer base and reducing customer concentration by pursuing qualification of additional buyers and developing overseas markets through the wholly owned subsidiary Alufluoride International Pte. Ltd., Singapore
- Evaluating other domestic and overseas growth opportunities including potential second-site AlF3 capacity, adjacent fluorine-derivative chemistries, transport of the Company's raw materials via Electric Vehicles, and value-added products from silica (a byproduct of AlF3 manufacture) - all at an assessment stage pending Board satisfaction on project specifications, capital cost, financing and revenue economics
- Continuing the phased capacity build-out at Visakhapatnam to match the medium-term capacity expansion trajectory announced by principal smelter customers
- Deploying retained earnings primarily towards capacity expansion, backward integration and strengthening of the working-capital position, alongside a policy of progressively growing shareholder distributions
- Maintaining captive solar power generation to keep conversion cost low and contain the Company's carbon footprint
- Exited the AlF3 joint venture in Jordan (withdrawal initiated FY2024-25, completed during FY2025-26) in response to the deteriorating West Asia political environment and a Jordanian-bank requirement for a parent corporate guarantee

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company has expanded its AlF3 manufacturing capacity at Visakhapatnam in phases: 4,000 TPA at commissioning; 8,000 TPA through debottlenecking over the years; 12,000 TPA in a second phase; 18,000 TPA in a subsequent debottlenecking; and 24,000 TPA on completion of the final phase in June 2026. A further expansion of AlF3 production infrastructure, undertaken in anticipation of increased FSA (raw material) availability, was targeted for completion by end of June 2026 and is stated to give the enhanced facility a production capacity of 80 tons per day (TPD). Separately, the Company is exploring a greenfield Alumina Hydrate manufacturing facility as a backward-integration and diversification project (objects clause amended via postal ballot on 20 April 2025), and is evaluating other domestic and overseas opportunities including potential second-site AlF3 capacity, adjacent fluorine-derivative chemistries, transport of raw materials via Electric Vehicles, and value-added products from silica (an AlF3 byproduct) - all at an early assessment stage. On the raw-material supply side, Coromandel International's new phosphoric acid plant at Kakinada began supplying FSA to the Company from April 2026, diversifying the supplier base alongside the existing long-term IFFCO Paradeep arrangement. The captive solar power facility (3 MW commissioned in 2021) was expanded by a further 1.1 MW to 4.1 MW in May 2026. During the year, Punjab National Bank sanctioned an additional term loan of INR 20.22 crore to fund further expansion of AlF3 production facilities.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Only manufacturer of AlF3 in Andhra Pradesh and one of the few domestic producers qualified to supply high-purity, low-bulk-density material to every major primary aluminium smelter in India, including Hindalco, Vedanta and NALCO
- High switching barriers: smelter qualification is a slow, exacting process, and an off-specification consignment can damage potlines that are expensive and time-consuming to restart, so established supplier relationships, quality consistency and delivery reliability - not price alone - determine retention of business
- External validation of customer standing: Hindalco Resilient Supply Chain Award (November 2024) and NALCO Best Customer (Chemical Division) Award (March 2025)
- Coastal Visakhapatnam plant location within manageable freight range of every major Indian smelter and on the same coast as both principal FSA suppliers, keeping outbound logistics efficient
- Captive solar power (expanded to 4.1 MW in May 2026) lowers the cost of conversion and the Company's carbon footprint

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Raw-material (FSA) supply concentration and geopolitical exposure — FSA, the Company's key raw material, is sourced principally from IFFCO Paradeep and supplemented by Paradeep Phosphates and Coromandel International's phosphoric acid plants; all suppliers ultimately depend on imported rock phosphate, sulphur and ammonia routed via the Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea. Intensifying West Asia hostilities have, since late FY2025-26, constrained the upstream sulphur/ammonia chain and the downstream FSA byproduct, forcing the Company to disclose a production scale-back to exchanges on 23 May 2026 with a financial impact management calls 'not presently determinable'.
- Customer concentration — Primary aluminium smelting capacity has consolidated among fewer, larger operators; the largest customer accounted for 69.27% of AlF3 revenue in FY2024-25, up sharply from 52.51% in FY2023-24, while the share from other 10%+ customers (excluding the top two) fell from 20.40% to nil, leaving the Company reliant on a small number of buyers.
- Single-product / single-activity concentration — The Company manufactures a single product line, Aluminium Fluoride, with no separate segment reporting under Ind AS 108; the ancillary solar power activity is immaterial to revenue and entirely dependent on captive consumption, leaving overall performance tied to one product and its input/output market dynamics.
- Cyclicality of the primary aluminium industry — Demand for AlF3 is transmitted through customers' offtake patterns in the primary aluminium industry, exposing the Company to that industry's cyclicality even though its own qualification-based customer relationships are sticky.
- Freight and logistics cost exposure — A portion of the Company's FSA requirement is moved over a longer distance from Odisha, and the associated inland freight cost is absorbed by the Company rather than passed through, an increase in which is flagged as a recurring risk.
- Input cost inflation (fuel, power, consumables) and foreign-exchange volatility — The Company is exposed to increases in the cost of fuel, power and consumables, and to foreign-exchange volatility on the limited proportion of imported inputs and capital goods.
- Operational hazard risk (fire, environmental incident, industrial accident) — Management flags the customary risks of fire, environmental incident and industrial accident at its manufacturing operations as a recurring risk category, against which it maintains insurance cover; the Board's overall view is that no material risk threatens the Company's existence.
